chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudayla ibn Ayyub from Aban from Ubayd Allah al-Halabi said: In the Qunut of Friday, [one says]: 'O Allah, bless Muhammad and the Imams of the Muslims. O Allah, make me among those You created for Your religion and among those You created for Your Paradise.' I said: 'Do I name the Imams?' He said: 'Name them collectively.' And - from him, from some of our companions, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The Qunut on Friday is in the first rak'ah after the recitation. You say in the Qunut: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them and

And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have guided us through it. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have honored us through it. O Allah, make us among those You chose for Your religion and created for Your Paradise. O Allah, 'do not deviate our hearts after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself a mercy, indeed You are the Bestower.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The family of the Prophet (implied in 'Al Muhammad')
key_terms.رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ: Lord of the Great Throne (Quranic phrase)
key_terms.قُنُوت: Supplication recited during prayer, specifically before or after bowing
key_terms.لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا: Do not deviate our hearts (Quranic phrase from Surah Al Imran)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for the Qunut of Friday prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific Qunut supplications for Friday prayer, emphasizing the inclusion of the Imams alongside the Prophet Muhammad, a key Shia theological distinction. The text prescribes reciting divine attributes and blessings before concluding with the Quranic verse 3:8, highlighting the continuity between prophetic guidance and the Imams' role in preserving the faith. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the Imams as the rightful successors and sources of religious authority.
